item.title: This week in science: anxiety in college students, potatoes on the moon and whale snot
item.description: Science reporters Nate Rott and Sanden Totten talk about the growing risk of anxiety among college students, a simulation of growing potatoes on the Moon, and the genetic secrets in whale snot.
item.content:encoded: Science reporters Nate Rott and Sanden Totten talk about the growing risk of anxiety among college students, a simulation of growing potatoes on the Moon, and the genetic secrets in whale snot.

item.title: Invading armies, subterfuge and conquest: How fire ant wars affect ecosystems
item.description: Ants disperse seeds, scavenge, turn soil and serve as a food source in their ecosystems. If local ants are displaced by invasive ants from elsewhere, the effects are widely felt.
item.content:encoded: Ants disperse seeds, scavenge, turn soil and serve as a food source in their ecosystems. If local ants are displaced by invasive ants from elsewhere, the effects are widely felt.

item.title: 'Medicare for all' is back on the drawing board. Does it stand a better chance this time?
item.description: Several newly elected Democratic U.S. senators campaigned on Medicare for All. Could this be the time it actually gets traction?

item.title: Scientists sequenced a whale's entire genome using drones and whale snot
item.description: Scientists were able to sequence the entire genome of a whale using samples of its snot. They used sharp flying skills and commercial drones affixed with petri dishes to collect the samples.

item.title: More people are getting the flu. Should you get a flu shot before you travel?
item.description: Thanksgiving is just around the corner, just as millions of Americans are expected to travel for the holidays. Another thing that's upon us? Cold and flu season.

item.title: Brain cell mapping lays groundwork for better treatments for conditions like dementia
item.description: A major effort from brain researchers around the world has yielded a cellular atlas of the basal ganglia — structures key to learning and controlling motor skills.

item.title: Far from home, Voyager 1 will soon be a 'light-day' from Earth
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1, which is the furthest human-made object from Earth, is set to reach a new milestone this week. On Wednesday, the probe will be roughly 16 billion miles from Earth.

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
item.description: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.

item.title: SpaceX deploys Starlink satellites in Starship test, but booster crashes into Gulf
item.description: SpaceX conducted a major test of its Starship rocket Friday night. It deployed several satellites for the Starlink constellation, but there was a problem with its booster.
